item.title: Video: NAFDAC uncovers suspected counterfeit whisky factory in Aba
item.description: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) says it has uncovered a suspected counterfeit alcoholic drinks factory in Aba, Abia State, with equipment and materials recovered from the facility estimated to be worth more than ₦500 million. The agency said the facility, located at No. 25 Omenazu Street, was discovered following credible intelligence about suspected illegal production activities. In a statement posted on X on Monday, NAFDAC said its officials found the facility operating under unhygienic conditions. It added that the suspected operator fled when the enforcement team arrived, abandoning a vehicle containing materials bearing the names of Sir Edwards Scotch Whisky and Scottish Hills Whisky. NAFDAC said further searches inside the facility led to the discovery of materials and equipment allegedly used in the production and packaging of the suspected counterfeit drinks. According to the agency, the items included bottle caps, sealing machines, empty bottles, cartons, packaging materials and tanks containing different liquid concoctions. Officials also found dirty sieves reportedly used in the production process, as well as plastic buckets and 200-litre drums containing ethanol. “Drums containing ethanol and tree bark immersed in ethanol were also discovered,” NAFDAC said, adding that the findings raised serious concerns about the safety and quality of the products allegedly being manufactured at the facility. The agency put the estimated value of the equipment, materials and other components recovered from the facility at more than ₦500 million. NAFDAC urged members of the public to assist its enforcement efforts by providing credible information about suspected illegal manufacturing operations. “The Agency urges members of the public to provide credible information on suspected illegal manufacturing activities to the NAFDAC,” the statement said. item.title: Uduaghan was a detribalised leader – Oborevwori
item.description: Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, has expressed sadness over the death of former Governor Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, CON, describing him as a detribalised leader whose contributions to the development of the state would not be forgotten. Uduaghan died on Monday, October 19, 2026, at the age of 71, according to a statement issued by his family. In a condolence message issued by his Chief Press Secretary, Sir Festus Ahon, Oborevwori sympathised with the late governor’s wife, Roli, his children, the entire Uduaghan family, the Itsekiri nation and Deltans over the painful loss. The governor recalled Uduaghan’s years in office, noting that he made significant contributions to infrastructure development in the state. He described the former governor as a leader who looked beyond ethnic differences and worked for the overall development of Delta State. Uduaghan served as Commissioner for Health from 1999 to 2003 and Secretary to the State Government from 2003 to 2007 before becoming governor in May 2007. He served two terms, leaving office in 2015. Oborevwori said Uduaghan’s years in public service had left a good mark on the state, adding that his death was a loss to Delta and the country at large. He prayed for the peaceful repose of the former governor’s soul and asked God to comfort his wife, children, family members, the Itsekiri nation and all those grieving his death. item.title: Ballon d’Or: Organisers unveil 3 criteria used to decide winner in 2026
item.description: With the 70th France Football Ballon d’Or ceremony approaching, attention is turning to the criteria jurors use to select the best male and female footballers of the year. The winners will be announced at the ceremony scheduled for October 26, 2026, in London, with individual performances, team achievements and sportsmanship forming the basis of the voting process. According to France Football’s official award regulations, the criteria are assessed in a specific order of importance, meaning they do not carry equal weight in the decision. Here are the three criteria used to determine the 2026 Ballon d’Or winners. 1. Individual performances, decisiveness and impressive displays Individual performances rank first among the three Ballon d’Or voting criteria. Jurors are expected to assess how well each nominee performed individually, including their influence on matches, consistency and ability to make a difference in important moments. This means a player’s overall contribution on the pitch is central to the assessment. Performances that help determine the outcome of matches are particularly relevant under this criterion. 2. Team performances and honours Team achievements rank second in the Ballon d’Or voting criteria. Jurors consider what nominees have accomplished with their clubs and national teams, including the honours they have won during the relevant period. Success in major competitions can therefore form part of the assessment, although team trophies are not the first criterion listed in the official regulations. The ranking places individual performances ahead of collective achievements when jurors evaluate the nominees. 3. Class and fair play Class and fair play rank third among the criteria. This criterion considers a player’s conduct and sportsmanship, including how they behave on the pitch and their respect for opponents, teammates, officials and the rules of the game. Although listed third, fair play remains part of the official assessment jurors must consider when deciding their rankings. Who votes for the Ballon d’Or? France Football’s voting system uses journalists selected according to the FIFA world rankings for the men’s and women’s national teams. For the men’s award, 100 journalists — one from each country represented in the top 100 of the men’s FIFA rankings — cast their votes. For the women’s award, 50 journalists — one from each country represented in the top 50 of the women’s FIFA rankings — participate in the voting. Each juror draws up a ranking of 10 nominees, following the award’s official rules. The voting process determines the final standings for the men’s and women’s awards, with the winners to be announced at the ceremony on October 26, 2026, in London. item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Opposition political parties and civil society organisations in Ebonyi State have condemned alleged threats, intimidation and harassment of opposition figures, critics and the media, demanding equal protection for all parties and candidates ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The parties rejected what they described as the politics of fear, insisting that the election should be decided on candidates’ records, competence, integrity and policy proposals rather than incumbency or the use of state machinery. It endorsed the candidacy of Dr Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii of the PDP, describing him as a credible alternative to lead the state. The communiqué also outlined six priority areas it said should form the minimum development agenda for any party seeking the mandate of Ebonyi residents. They include fiscal transparency and accountability, economic diversification, the transformation of agriculture into agro-industry, mining reform, human capital development and an improved business environment, as well as infrastructure development. On infrastructure, the summit proposed the construction of 200 kilometres of critical farm-to-market roads, dedicated power supply for industrial clusters and expanded broadband access to support electronic governance and e-commerce. The organisers subsequently relocated the gathering to another hotel, where the proceedings took place. The circumstances surrounding the reported barricade and the identities of those involved were not independently established in the information provided. item.title: Emir’s Murder: Osun police declare two ex-NURTW chiefs wanted
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State Police Command has declared two former chieftains of the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Wakili Nurudeen, popularly known as Alowonle, and Olayemi Ojo, alias Sibi, wanted in connection with the murder of Dauda Oyeyemi, also known as Emir. The Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, disclosed this on Monday while addressing journalists at the command’s headquarters in Osogbo, where six other suspects linked to the killing were paraded. Emir was killed on Sunday, September 13, 2026, at Mayfair Motor Park, Ile-Ife, by masked gunmen amid a reported succession dispute among members of the transport union. Zungura said investigations by the police homicide section led to the arrest of two NURTW members, Waliu Adejare, aka Jay Jay, Chairman of Aregbe Park, Osogbo, and Hammed Dauda, aka Jagaban, the park’s secretary. Four personnel of the Osun State Security Network Agency, popularly known as Amotekun, were also arrested in connection with the incident. They are Tijani Ismail, Akinsola Ekundayo, Sijuade Moruf and Ayeni Adegbola. The police commissioner said the arrests were made following investigations, with assistance from the state’s Amotekun commandant. He added that Dauda allegedly confessed that the cut-to-size firearm found in his possession had been given to him by Alowonle. The four Amotekun personnel, according to the police, had been seconded to provide security for the former NURTW chairman. Zungura said further investigations led to Adejare’s arrest, adding that the suspects were allegedly mobilised by Alowonle and Ojo. “I hereby declare Wakili Nurudeen, aka Alowonle, and Olayemi Ojo, alias Sibi, wanted in connection with the murder. They maintained that the most effective way to build a formidable presidential campaign organisation was to work through established party structures rather than introduce arrangements capable of generating internal divisions. The dispute also extends to the distribution of campaign resources, with the chairmen demanding that vehicles, branded equipment, publicity materials, logistical support and other mobilisation items be released to them for deployment across their respective states. They argued that the recognised state leadership possessed the organisational capacity to distribute the materials transparently and according to local political realities. “We maintain that campaign resources are most effective when entrusted to recognised party structures that possess the capacity to deploy them strategically, transparently, and in accordance with the peculiar needs of each state,” they stated. The chairmen further appealed to Bauchi State Governor, Senator Bala Mohammed, whom they described as the party’s national leader, and Makinde to intervene urgently to resolve the disagreement. They warned that continued operation of parallel campaign structures without due regard for recognised state chairmen could generate unnecessary tension and undermine the progress already recorded by the party. While expressing support for the proposed presidential campaign, the South-East leaders cautioned that their continued participation in the present arrangement could not be taken for granted if their concerns were ignored. “Most importantly, we unequivocally state that, should these grievances not be addressed immediately and satisfactorily, the undersigned State Chairmen may be compelled to reconsider their continued participation in the present campaign arrangement and take further appropriate decisions in the collective political interest of their respective states and the South-East geopolitical zone,” they warned. The communiqué also raised concerns about the proposed town hall meetings being organised to promote the party’s RESET NIGERIA AGENDA, particularly the approach to mobilising participants in the South-East. item.title: Christiane Amanpour announces exit from CNN after 43 years
item.description: Veteran journalist Christiane Amanpour has announced plans to leave CNN in June 2027, ending a 43-year association with the international news network. The 68-year-old chief international anchor announced her decision on Monday, describing her time at CNN as “43 fantastic years” and expressing enthusiasm for new professional opportunities. “Remember: always be truthful, not neutral,” Amanpour said in a statement, reflecting the journalistic principle that has guided her career. Amanpour has presented her flagship interview programme on CNN International since 2009, interviewing influential political figures and reporting from some of the world’s major conflict zones. Her departure will follow a gradual reduction in her presenting duties. She scaled back her schedule in January 2025 and is expected to transition to a weekly programme format in January 2027. The show is scheduled to end in May, while she will continue reporting for CNN until June. CNN chairman Mark Thompson said he had held discussions with Amanpour about her plans for several months. He praised her standing in the profession, describing her as “one of the most trusted and beloved journalists anywhere.” Thompson also commended her decades of international reporting, adding that CNN would recognise her contributions before she leaves the network. Looking back on her career, Amanpour cited her coverage of major global events, including the First Gulf War, the Bosnian War, the genocide in Rwanda, the conflicts in Afghanistan and Ukraine, and developments in Iran. She also acknowledged the journalists, programme teams and field crews who had worked with her over the years. According to Amanpour, their collective dedication to facts, evidence and humanity helped shape her approach to reporting. Although she is preparing to leave her regular role at CNN, Amanpour said she remained committed to the network’s mission of independent journalism as she looks towards the next phase of her career. item.title: Fire guts 33,000-litre tanker under Otedola Bridge
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Panic gripped motorists and passers-by on Monday after a 33,000-litre tanker conveying petroleum products caught fire under Otedola Bridge along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The incident reportedly occurred at about 3pm when the tanker, which was transporting petroleum products from a depot, fell between the inward and outward sections of the bridge and burst into flames. The fire caused panic among motorists, who diverted to avoid the scene, while passers-by scampered in different directions for safety. Men of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service from the Alausa and Ikeja fire stations were immediately deployed to the scene to contain the fire. Their prompt intervention prevented the situation from escalating, while damping-down operations continued as of 5pm to extinguish residual hotspots and prevent possible re-ignition. As of press time, the immediate and remote causes of the incident had yet to be established. No casualties or property damage were recorded, according to the available report. The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Mrs Margaret Adeseye, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to protecting lives and property through prompt and effective emergency response. She urged motorists to exercise caution around emergency scenes and comply with safety instructions issued by emergency responders. item.title: Tinubu: APC campaign council consults 4 northern emirs, seeks prayers
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Director General of the All Progressives Congress APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has taken the Council’s 2027 consultations to four northern emirates, telling the royal fathers he came to seek their prayers and blessings and not their political endorsements. He led a delegation of national leaders on Monday, 19th October 2026, to the Emirs of Gwandu, Katsina, Daura and Zaria. The delegation left the Private Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, at 11am and was received at each of the four palaces later in the day. The royal fathers offered prayers and blessings for peace, unity and the success of the nation’s democratic journey. Yari said the Council’s engagement with traditional institutions was a cornerstone of its consultative strategy. He said the delegation came to seek the prayers, blessings and counsel of the emirs, whose moral and spiritual guidance, he added, remains indispensable to the nation’s political process. The visits form part of a wider tour of traditional and political leaders across the country. The Council said it was building consensus and galvanising support ahead of key campaign activities leading up to 16th January 2027, which it described as “a significant date in the electoral calendar.” The Council reaffirmed its respect for Nigeria’s traditional institutions and their role in fostering peace, unity and stability. It said it remained committed to carrying all stakeholders along in the build-up to the 2027 general elections. The delegation included the Kebbi state Governor, Dr Nasiru Idris; Zamfara governor, Dauda Lawal; Senator Ali Modu Sheriff, Dr. Abdullahi Umar Ganduje, Senator Adamu Aliero, Senator Sani Ahmad Yarima and Senator Aliyu Magatakarda Wamakko. Others were Senator Muhammad Danjuma Goje, Barrister Ibrahim Shehu Shema, Rt. Hon. Aminu Bello Masari, Senator Rochas Owelle Okorocha and Muhammad Badaru Abubakar. Also on the team were Senator Simon Lalong, Rt. Hon. Sabur Oladimeji Bankole, Senators Yahaya Abdullahi and Francis Adenigba Fadahunsi. The delegation was completed by Hon. San Marino — 61 square kilometres San Marino is a landlocked microstate surrounded by Italy, with an area of approximately 61 square kilometres. item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced her separation from her husband and fellow tennis star Gaël Monfils, saying the emotional toll of Russia’s war on Ukraine left her feeling she was “slowly losing” herself. Svitolina, 32, shared the news in an emotional Instagram statement on Monday, describing sleepless nights, self-doubt and the difficulty of deciding to end their marriage. She said Monfils had supported her through the hardest moments, but she had come to realise she needed to find her way back to herself outside the marriage. “This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share,” she wrote. “Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me. What I have rarely spoken about is what the war has done to me inside. Last year, I told you I needed to step away from the court because I wasn’t in the right emotional space. Today, I want to open up a little more. What you didn’t see were the sleepless nights, the doubts, and the feeling of slowly losing myself. “Gaël saw all of it. He never let go of my hand. We fought through this together for a long time, with everything we had. But some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you. “With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage. It is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love. Gaël listened. He has respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget. Svitolina stressed that the separation was not the result of blame or a lack of love. She described it as a painful decision made after the couple had tried to face her struggles together, and said Monfils had respected what she needed. “Gaël has loved me through my greatest joys and my darkest moments, and I have loved him with all my heart. Together, we built a beautiful life, and we were given the most precious gift of all, our daughter, Skai. “Skai will always come first. Our marriage is ending, but our family is not. We will always be her parents, side by side, at every step of her life. “Please know that there is no one to blame here. There are only two people who loved each other deeply and a story that is changing shape. “We ask for your kindness and for the space we need to heal. “Thank you for your love.” Svitolina and Monfils married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter, Skai. They also partnered in the US Open mixed doubles earlier this year, reaching the semi-finals before losing to Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli. Svitolina, a four-time Grand Slam semi-finalist, most recently competed at the Wuhan Open, where Britain’s Sonay Kartal beat her in a three-set quarter-final. Monfils, 40, is a former world No 6. According to Ogeah, Uduaghan’s background as a medical doctor and administrator helped him drive the initiative with considerable commitment. “The initiative revolutionised health services in Nigeria because it was unknown in the country. His background as an accomplished medical practitioner and administrator equipped him for the project, and he drove it with immense passion,” he said. On education, Ogeah recalled that Uduaghan built modern classrooms and equipped science laboratories across the state. He also highlighted the EduMarshal project, which was introduced to ensure that school-age children attended classes during school hours. Under the initiative, parents of children found hawking on the streets during school hours were apprehended and prosecuted, he said. Ogeah added that Uduaghan established a scholarship scheme for Delta State indigenes who graduated from Nigerian universities with first-class degrees, awarding each beneficiary N5 million to pursue further studies anywhere in the world. Describing Uduaghan’s economic vision, the former commissioner said the governor’s “Delta Beyond Oil” initiative reflected his understanding of the need to reduce the state’s dependence on crude oil revenue and develop other sectors of the economy. “Nigerians got to know that crude oil, which remains the mainstay of the economy, is a finite resource that has a limited life span. He began the process of weaning Delta’s economy from dependence on oil and growing other sectors of the economy,” Ogeah said. He added that Uduaghan’s emphasis on economic diversification anticipated the need for governments at all levels to prepare for the eventual depletion of crude oil resources. On infrastructure, Ogeah identified the construction and operationalisation of Asaba International Airport as one of Uduaghan’s signature projects, saying it opened up Delta North to greater development. He recalled that he personally contributed to securing some of the approvals required for the airport’s operations through contacts in the aviation sector following his tenure as managing director of Sahcol. Ogeah also cited the construction of the Government House in Asaba, stadiums in Warri and Sapele, and the Stephen Keshi Stadium as major infrastructure projects undertaken during Uduaghan’s administration. The Stephen Keshi Stadium later hosted international matches and served as the main venue for the 21st National Sports Festival in 2022. He further praised the late governor’s approach to the distribution of infrastructure projects across the state, citing the Trans-Warri–Ode-Itsekiri Road and Bridge project, which included the construction of bridges linking riverine communities. In the health sector, he said Uduaghan established specialist facilities at the Mother and Child Hospital in Warri and the Delta State University Teaching Hospital in Oghara, including diagnostic equipment. Ogeah added that the former governor invested in media development by sponsoring journalists from print and electronic media organisations in Delta State for specialised training at the Thomson Reuters Foundation Institute in London. He said more than 40 practising journalists benefited from the programme. Expressing gratitude for the opportunity to have worked with Uduaghan, Ogeah extended his condolences to the former governor’s wife and children. “I was greatly inspired by Dr Uduaghan’s sense of service to the people. It was a great privilege to have worked closely with him. I commiserate with his wife and children. He was a great boss I will always cherish. May God receive him in His paradise,” he said. item.title: Delta Abure-led Labour Party reaffirms alliance with AAC ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: The Abure-aligned faction of the Labour Party in Delta State has reaffirmed its political alliance with the African Action Congress (AAC) ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that its endorsement of the party’s governorship candidate, Engr. Isaac O. Eshor, and other AAC candidates remains valid. The state chapter, led by Hon. Okwuokei Vincent Ikechukwu, made the position known in a press statement in which it disowned a social media publication purportedly seeking to discredit the alliance and its endorsement of AAC candidates. The faction said the publication did not reflect its official position, describing it as unauthorised and capable of creating confusion among party members, supporters and the general public. It maintained that the decision to work with the AAC was deliberate and formed part of its political strategy for the 2027 elections. According to the statement, the Labour Party structure aligned with Barr. Julius Abure in Delta State is committed to collaborating with the AAC to build what it described as a viable political alternative capable of challenging the existing political order. The faction also reaffirmed its loyalty to Abure and the leadership structure recognised by its members, urging the public to distinguish between authorised communications from its leadership and publications issued without its approval. It further stated that the alliance was intended to mobilise support for AAC candidates contesting the governorship, National Assembly and Delta State House of Assembly elections. The statement added that the faction would continue to engage with like-minded political stakeholders, stressing that misinformation and political controversies would not distract it from its preparations for the 2027 general elections. The Abure-aligned faction also urged its members, support groups, youth organisations, market women and campaign volunteers to remain calm and seek clarification from its recognised leadership whenever conflicting information emerged. It called on political stakeholders to exercise restraint and avoid circulating unverified claims capable of generating confusion within the state’s political landscape. The statement also asserted that the Abure-aligned structure had no legal political link with the faction associated with Senator Nenadi Usman, claiming that the latter had no political structure in Delta State. Reaffirming its position, the faction said its alliance with the AAC and support for Eshor and other AAC candidates would be pursued through lawful, peaceful and democratic means. The statement was signed by Okwuokei Vincent Ikechukwu, state chairman of the Labour Party (Abure faction), Delta State Chapter, on behalf of the State Executive Committee. item.title: Thierry Henry, Kate Scott confirmed as hosts of 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Thierry Henry and Kate Scott have been confirmed as hosts of the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, which will take place at London’s Palladium on Monday, October 26. The event will mark the 70th edition of the awards and bring together leading figures in world football. Henry, a 1998 World Cup and 2009 Champions League winner, finished second in the Ballon d’Or voting in 2003 and was nominated nine times during his playing career. The former Arsenal striker will present the ceremony alongside British journalist Scott, who regularly works with Henry on CBS Sports’ Champions League coverage. Henry explained that he was honoured to have been asked to present the ceremony in the city. He said, ‘London is the city I call home, and I have a deep connection to its football culture and the passionate fans here, so to be hosting here alongside my friend and colleague Kate feels like a natural fit.’ Henry and Scott both appear on CBS Sports Golazo during Champions League coverage, alongside Jamie Carragher and Micah Richards. The men’s shortlist includes current holder Ousmane Dembélé, eight-time winner Lionel Messi and 2024 winner Rodri. Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal, Erling Haaland and Arsenal’s Declan Rice, Gabriel and William Saliba are also among the nominees. Alexia Putellas, a two-time winner, is the only former champion on the women’s shortlist. Arsenal forwards Mariona Caldentey and Alessia Russo are among the nominees, alongside Barcelona stars Caroline Graham Hansen, Ewa Pajor and Clàudia Pina. Men’s Ballon d’Or nominees Jude Bellingham, Pau Cubarsí, Marc Cucurella, Ousmane Dembélé, Luis Díaz, Bruno Fernandes, Gabriel, Erling Haaland, Achraf Hakimi, Harry Kane, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Lamine Yamal, Sadio Mané, Marquinhos, Lautaro Martínez, Kylian Mbappé, Nuno Mendes, Lionel Messi, João Neves, Michael Olise, Willian Pacho, Julián Quiñones, Declan Rice, Rodri, Fabián Ruiz, William Saliba, Ferran Torres, Dayot Upamecano, Vinícius Júnior and Vitinha. item.title: Alausa tightens recruitment controls in Federal universities
item.description: …Orders VCs to Justify New Courses With Job-Market Demand By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has tightened recruitment controls in federal universities, directing vice-chancellors to justify manpower requests based on staffing needs, labour-market demand and national human capital development priorities. The directive, issued by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, comes amid concerns over rising manpower requests by tertiary institutions and the financial burden such demands place on the Federal Government’s personnel budget. Under the new guidelines, federal universities are to prioritise filling vacancies arising from staff attrition, while requests for additional recruitment to support new courses, programmes or institutional expansion will face stricter scrutiny. In a letter dated October 19, 2026, addressed to vice-chancellors of all federal universities, Alausa expressed concern that many institutions submitted manpower requests without adequately considering the financial implications for the Federal Government. He said the existing arrangement had disconnected universities’ manpower demands from the additional personnel costs, which are borne entirely by the Federal Government. The minister also faulted requests for additional staff to support courses that do not adequately respond to Nigeria’s labour-market needs. According to him, some requests are not aligned with national human capital development priorities or existing skills gaps in the labour market. To address the concerns, Alausa directed vice-chancellors to ensure that all manpower requests undergo strict vetting under two categories: vacancies arising from staff attrition and requests for additional recruitment. Under the first category, institutions are expected to seek approval to fill vacancies resulting from retirement, resignation, death, dismissal or transfer of existing personnel. However, requests for recruitment beyond replacing departing staff must meet additional requirements. The minister said universities seeking additional personnel for new courses, programmes or expansion must provide clear evidence of market demand, graduate employability and the programmes’ relevance to Nigeria’s human capital development. They must also demonstrate that proposed courses are unique and do not duplicate programmes already offered by other institutions. The directive places greater emphasis on justifying additional staffing, particularly where universities seek to recruit personnel for academic programmes whose relevance to national development or employment opportunities may be questioned. Alausa said the measures were necessary to promote prudence, efficiency and strategic manpower planning across the education sector, urging vice-chancellors to comply fully with the new requirements. The directive, issued by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, comes amid concerns over rising manpower requests by tertiary institutions and the financial burden such demands place on the Federal Government’s personnel budget. Under the new guidelines, federal universities are to prioritise filling vacancies arising from staff attrition, while requests for additional recruitment to support new courses, programmes or institutional expansion will face stricter scrutiny. In a letter dated October 19, 2026, addressed to vice-chancellors of all federal universities, Alausa expressed concern that many institutions submitted manpower requests without adequately considering the financial implications for the Federal Government. He said the existing arrangement had disconnected universities’ manpower demands from the additional personnel costs, which are borne entirely by the Federal Government. The minister also faulted requests for additional staff to support courses that do not adequately respond to Nigeria’s labour-market needs. According to him, some requests are not aligned with national human capital development priorities or existing skills gaps in the labour market. To address the concerns, Alausa directed vice-chancellors to ensure that all manpower requests undergo strict vetting under two categories: vacancies arising from staff attrition and requests for additional recruitment. Under the first category, institutions are expected to seek approval to fill vacancies resulting from retirement, resignation, death, dismissal or transfer of existing personnel. However, requests for recruitment beyond replacing departing staff must meet additional requirements. The minister said universities seeking additional personnel for new courses, programmes or expansion must provide clear evidence of market demand, graduate employability and the programmes’ relevance to Nigeria’s human capital development. They must also demonstrate that proposed courses are unique and do not duplicate programmes already offered by other institutions. The directive places greater emphasis on justifying additional staffing, particularly where universities seek to recruit personnel for academic programmes whose relevance to national development or employment opportunities may be questioned. Alausa said the measures were necessary to promote prudence, efficiency and strategic manpower planning across the education sector, urging vice-chancellors to comply fully with the new requirements. Copies of the directive were sent to the Minister of Finance, Minister of State for Education, Accountant-General of the Federation, Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Education, Executive Secretary of the National Universities Commission, Director-General of the Budget Office and Chairman of the Federal Character Commission, among other officials. item.title: Lagos shuts Ejigbo Fire Station after alleged assault
item.description: By Evelyn Usman The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service has indefinitely closed its Ejigbo Fire Station following reported repeated assaults on its personnel, calling for an impartial investigation into the incidents. The Service said the decision was taken to protect firefighters and firefighting equipment after personnel were allegedly attacked at the station on Tuesday, October 13, and again on Friday, October 16, 2026. According to the Service, the first incident was reported to the Ejigbo Police Station. However, the alleged assailants reportedly returned days later and disrupted operations despite the intervention of senior police authorities. The Controller-General of the Service, Mrs Margaret Adeseye, condemned the reported attacks, warning that violence against emergency responders could undermine public safety and effective emergency service delivery. In a statement, Adeseye said the incidents had raised serious concerns about the safety of firefighters and other emergency responders responsible for protecting lives and property across Lagos State. She stressed that personnel must be able to perform their statutory duties without fear of violence, intimidation or unlawful interference. “Attacks on emergency responders can compromise operational readiness, delay emergency interventions and expose members of the public to avoidable risks,” she said. Adeseye said the Ejigbo station would remain closed indefinitely pending a satisfactory resolution of the matter. She added that personnel and firefighting equipment attached to the station would be temporarily redeployed to an undisclosed location for security reasons. According to her, the measure is intended to safeguard personnel and equipment while ensuring continuity of emergency response operations in the affected area. The Controller-General urged relevant security agencies to conduct a thorough, impartial and professional investigation to establish the facts and take appropriate action, in accordance with the law, against anyone found responsible. Reaffirming the Service’s commitment to protecting lives and property across Lagos State, Adeseye said it would continue to work with relevant authorities to address the security concerns and ensure that firefighters could operate in a safe environment.
